verdict.rationale: Cal.com's AI-native positioning is entirely about exposing itself AS an MCP server/tool provider (mcp.cal.com, API v2 for agents) so that external AI agents can call Cal.com's scheduling tools — the evidence shows no agentic host/orchestration role within Cal.com where a user would plug external MCP servers into Cal.com itself to extend its own capabilities. This story describes the client-side 'consume other tools' direction, which is a different axis (and the inverse of what Cal.com's docs describe), so it is a category mismatch for this SaaS scheduling product's documented architecture.
